card: Encapsulates CTransaction data members behind public observer methods (such as GetInputs() and GetOutputs()) and makes the underlying members private. Callers across the codebase currently access public members directly, freezing the internal layout into the public API and preventing representations like shared block state or immutable transaction buffers. The mechanical migration across 94 files was automated via a custom bitcoin-tidy check included in the PR. This encapsulation supports broader interface segregation efforts, including the proposed stateless validation library in #35904.
changed_since_previous: Replaced remaining occurrences of `decltype(CTransaction::version)` with explicit `uint32_t` in policy and RPC code.
evidence: Description: 'Public data members make the representation of a type part of its API. Once access goes through observers, the representation can change without requiring its users to change as well. Potential changes are using shared immutable transaction state, or even an offset into shared immutable block state.'
Description: 'This work is part of the broader interface-segregation direction described in #35904, but is not a prerequisite for the stateless validation library proposed there.'
problem: Public data members on `CTransaction` bake the internal storage layout directly into the public API across the entire codebase. This prevents altering the underlying representation (such as referencing shared block data or shared immutable transaction memory) and hinders separating serialization and validation functionality.

risk.why: A copy or reference mismatch in accessor calls in consensus or script validation paths could cause performance regressions or validation failures across the node.

scope_notes: Large mechanical change touching 94 files, automated with a newly introduced clang-tidy check (`contrib/devtools/bitcoin-tidy/use-observers.cpp`).
summary: Encapsulates `CTransaction` data members behind public `const` observer methods (such as `GetInputs()` and `GetOutputs()`) and makes the underlying member variables private. Callers throughout the codebase are migrated to the new observers using a newly introduced `bitcoin-tidy` check. Matching observer methods are also added to `CMutableTransaction` to support generic code.
